seo.title: Ship Design Brief | Start a Vessel Design Project | LASAN MARINE
seo.description: A simple design brief for sharing the vessel mission, expected dimensions, hull material, propulsion and other known requirements before concept development begins.

fields.headline: Start with what you already know
fields.lead: At the beginning of a project, you may only have the vessel mission, an expected size, a hull material or an engine in mind. The design brief collects those early decisions in one place so we can understand the project faster and focus the first design discussion.

fields.label: DESIGN BRIEF
fields.heading: You do not need every answer before you start
fields.intro: Add the vessel type, mission, expected dimensions, hull material, main engine or any other requirement already known. Leave uncertain items blank. We can work through them as the concept develops.

fields.heading: Common questions when preparing a design brief

items.title: Can I submit the brief if I do not know the exact vessel dimensions?
items.content: Yes. You can provide a target range, known constraints or leave the dimensions open. Principal dimensions can be developed as part of the concept stage.

items.title: Is the design brief a design document?
items.content: No. It is an input document used to establish the project requirements before detailed calculations and drawings begin.

items.title: Can I use the brief for a vessel conversion?
items.content: Yes. Describe the intended change and attach any existing drawings, vessel data or photos you have. Those references help us understand which parts of the vessel may be affected.

items.title: What happens after I send the brief?
items.content: We review the information, identify any critical gaps and come back with the calculations, drawings or design work we believe the project needs next.

fields.heading: From brief to first design decisions
fields.content: Once the key requirements are captured, we can review the brief and discuss the concept, the calculations that matter and the technical documentation needed for the next stage.
